# Citations

Sources fetched in-session for [international rental property for a US
investor](international-rental-property.md). Every claim in the deliverable and
the [reference files](references/) cites a number from this list.

**Tier scale.** Tier 1 = government, statute, court, national statistics office,
intergovernmental body, peer-reviewed. Tier 2 = major law firm, established
reference site, statutory professional body, major news. Tier 3 = industry or
practitioner site. Tier 4 = forum, crowd-sourced, or a site with a direct
commercial stake in the answer.

**Access.** `OK` = page text retrieved and read. `FAILED` = the fetch was
attempted and recorded a failure; the claim it was meant to support is reported
as a gap, never filled from memory. Retrieval ran through a host-side fetch
service; several hosts refuse that service specifically, which is a property of
this run and not of the source.

## Tenancy law and possession recovery

**[30]** Chambre nationale des commissaires de justice, *Point presse logement*,
17 March 2026.
<https://commissaire-justice.fr/communiques/point-presse-logement-impayes-loyers-charges-de-coproprietes-et-tensions-sur-le-logement/>
**Tier:** 2 (statutory professional order) **Access:** OK
2025 vs 2024 volumes: 175,000 commandements de payer; 147,000 assignations;
30,500 executed evictions (+27.2%). **An incompressible minimum of 8 months**
between first arrears and eviction with police assistance, attributed by CNCJ to
Sénat *Rapport n° 278 (2022-2023)*, p. 46; CNCJ's own practitioner estimate that
a complete procedure runs "closer to two years"; hearing delays of 8–10 months in
large metropolitan courts. Kasbarian law of 27 July 2023 cut the
commandement-to-assignation interval from two months to six weeks, held
non-retroactive by a Cour de cassation *avis* of 13 June 2024, so two regimes
coexist.
**Source quality note:** the 8-month figure is second-hand; the Senate report
was not retrieved. The "two years" figure is expert judgement, not a
measurement.

**Source quality note:** the note's subtitle conflates share-of-total with

deducción alguna**." Mexican-resident payers withhold; where the payer is also
foreign-resident the owner self-assesses **within 15 days**; a fideicomiso
trustee withholds. Page last modified 5 April 2017 and carries its own
no-rights disclaimer.

**[40]** SAT, *Ficha 53/ISR — aviso de opción de no retención, residentes en
Estados Unidos*.
<https://www.sat.gob.mx/gobmx/Paginas/ficha_53_isr.html>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
A **US-resident-specific** annual notice, filed in January and February under
RMF rule 3.18.5, electing net-basis ISR on rental income. The resulting net-basis
rate is not stated on the page.

**[41]** DGI Panamá, *Generalidades de la Declaración del Impuesto Sobre la
Renta*.
<https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/DInforme/GD-ISR>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
Confirms rental income is Panamanian-source and lists deductible rental expenses
under art. 21 of Decreto Ejecutivo 98 de 2010 — property taxes, depreciation of
improvements, maintenance, **third-party management fees**, condominium charges,
insurance, bad debts over one year, and acquisition/improvement loan interest.
**States no rate applicable to an individual's rental income.**

**[42]** DGI Panamá, *ITBMS — servicios exentos*.
<https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/itbms/SE-Itbms>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
Residential leases are ITBMS-exempt where the contract term exceeds six months;
below that the letting is treated as non-residential and is subject to the tax.

**[43]** NAV, *Lakáskiadás* (2024.08.03).
<https://nav.gov.hu/Elethelyzetek-adozasa/vagyonugyek/Lakaskiadas>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
15% personal income tax on rental income, paid as quarterly advances by the 12th
of the following month; either a flat **10% cost deduction** or itemised costs
including depreciation; corporate or sole-trader tenants withhold; residential
letting is VAT-exempt with a HUF 12m threshold.
**Scope caveat:** the page addresses the general Hungarian rule and **never
mentions non-residents**.

**[44]** Autoridade Tributária, *Modelo 3, Anexo F — rendimentos prediais*
(model in force from January 2025, PDF).
<https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/apoio_contribuinte/modelos_formularios/irs/Documents/Mod_3_anexo_F.pdf>
*(URL corrected after the citation audit: an earlier draft cited a separate
`Mod_3_Anexo_F_Instrucoes.pdf` that was never fetched. The quoted content is
from the file above and is unchanged.)*
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
Rental income "tributados às taxas previstas no artigo 72.º do Código do IRS" —
the rate is cited, not stated. **Aggregation (englobamento) is available only to
residents**, so a US owner is locked into the art. 72 special rate. Withholding
columns confirm tenants who are withholding agents do withhold.

## US federal tax

**[45]** IRS, *Estate & gift tax treaties (international)*.
<https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estate-gift-tax-treaties-international>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
Current IRS list of countries with US estate and/or gift tax treaties. Of the
nine studied, **France, Greece and Italy appear; Costa Rica, Hungary, Spain,
Portugal, Mexico and Panama do not.**

**[46]** IRS, *Instructions for Form 706* (Rev. August 2014), Schedule P (PDF).
<https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i706--2014.pdf>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK (PDF text extracted)
Enumerated list of countries with death tax conventions in effect, corroborating
[45]. Mechanics: Form 706-CE required; separate computation per country;
conversion at the rate in effect when each foreign payment is made; where a
treaty exists the taxpayer may take whichever of treaty, statute, or treaty plus
statutory credit for political-subdivision taxes is most favourable.

**[47]** IRS, *Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements* (updated
18/09/2025).
<https://www.irs.gov/businesses/comparison-of-form-8938-and-fbar-requirements>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
"Foreign real estate held directly — [8938:] No — [FBAR:] No." Foreign real
estate held through a foreign entity: the entity interest is itself a specified
foreign financial asset valued inclusive of the real estate. Thresholds and the
independence of the two regimes.

**[48]** Cornell LII, *26 U.S. Code § 168*.
<https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/168>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
§168(g)(1)(A) mandates ADS for property "used predominantly outside the United
States"; §168(g)(2) prescribes straight line and a **30-year** recovery period
for residential rental property; §168(e)(2) defines residential rental property
by the 80%-of-gross-rental-income test; the TCJA effective-date note applies the
current table to property placed in service after 31 December 2017.

**[49]** Cornell LII, *26 U.S. Code § 2014* and *26 CFR § 20.2014-1*.
<https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2014> ·
<https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/20.2014-1>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
The unilateral foreign death tax credit available where no treaty exists: credit
only for taxes on property situated in, and taxed by, the foreign country and
included in the gross estate; two ratio limitations; no credit for interest or
penalties; four-year claim window; credit or deduction, not both.

**[50]** IRS, *United States income tax treaties — A to Z* (reviewed
03/01/2026).
<https://www.irs.gov/businesses/international-businesses/united-states-income-tax-treaties-a-to-z>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
Lists France, Greece, Italy, Mexico, Portugal and Spain. Carries the verbatim
entry "**Hungary – CAUTION Treaty Terminated**", without a date. Costa Rica and
Panama do not appear.

**[51]** IRS, *Internal Revenue Manual* 4.25.4.
<https://www.irs.gov/irm/part4/irm_04-025-004>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
States the double-taxation exposure in the IRS's own words: a US decedent's
estate "may face double taxation as a result of the decedent's ownership of
foreign property"; the credit covers all national and local foreign death taxes;
credit and deduction are alternatives; treaty positions require Form 8833.

Austria and Denmark seasonal and holiday homes are at least 40% of unoccupied

in every EU country **except Italy and Cyprus**; largest rise **Hungary +231%**.
Rents rose everywhere **except Greece (−16%)**; Hungary +107%. Hungarian
inflation over the same period 86%, Greek 20%. Housing cost overburden 2024:
Greece 29% in cities and 28% in rural areas, the EU's highest.

## Counter-evidence

**[60]** Miyakawa, D., Shimizu, C. & Uesugi, I., "Do Foreign Buyers Pay More
Than Domestic Buyers? Evidence from International Transaction-Level Data",
*Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics* 68, 394–424 (2024).
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11146-022-09937-6>
**Tier:** 1 (peer-reviewed, open access) **Access:** OK
About 28,500 usable transactions across eight countries including France: "foreign
investors pay significantly higher prices than domestic investors, even after
taking a wide variety of controls into account", with the premium shrinking as
the buyer's local exposure grows.
**Scope caveat:** investment and business property, not owner-occupier
residential; France is the only one of the nine in the sample; the authors note
the result weakens in the pre-crisis and non-business subsamples.

**[61]** Lepers, E., "Cross-border real estate investment: a different animal?",
*Review of World Economics* 160, 481–508 (2024).
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10290-023-00505-5>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK (abstract only; body paywalled)
Notes that cross-border real estate investment "has seen little research"
despite its financial-stability implications. Commercial, not residential.

**[62]** International Trade Administration, *Panama — Investment Climate
Statement* (country commercial guide), last published 27 March 2026.
<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/panama-investment-climate-statement>
**Tier:** 1 **Access:** OK
The only Investment Climate Statement content retrieved anywhere in this run.
Names as impediments to investment "corruption, insufficient transparency and
judicial capacity, **non-payment issues**, and an undereducated workforce".
Fiscal deficit 7.4% of GDP in 2024 against a 4.0% statutory target; debt $56.3bn
at April 2025, about 70% of GDP; **Fitch downgraded Panama to BB+,
non-investment grade, on 28 March 2024**; Moody's Baa3 and S&P BBB− at 9 June
2025.

## Sources sought and not obtained

Recorded because their absence shapes the deliverable's gaps. Each was fetched
and returned a recorded failure.

**[63]** US State Department, *Investment Climate Statements* — Costa Rica,
Mexico and Panama chapters across the 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2025 editions,
including the 2017-2021 and 2021-2025 archive mirrors and the two index pages. **Tier:** 1 **Access:** FAILED — every one returned HTTP 200 with the body "We're
sorry, this site is currently experiencing technical difficulties… Exception:
forbidden"; the Panama PDF failed to parse. Ten files in total.
Consequence: **no expropriation record, no investor-state case count and no
transfer-policy evidence exists in this run for any of the nine countries.**

rental pages, the non-resident income guide, and the property-purchase user

every URL.
Consequence: Greek tax rates, registration mechanics and property price levels
are absent. The one Greek source that answered is [25].

(AREAER), and the World Justice Project Rule of Law Index tables.

bodies.

rather than from CEPEJ directly.
